thread.title: Marijuana Stocks: MedMen Seeks Delivery, Expansion; Canopy Grows In Africa

author: BILL PETERS
title: Marijuana Stocks: MedMen Seeks Delivery, Expansion; Canopy Grows In Africa
text:
One of the newest marijuana stocks, MedMen, wants to offer weed delivery and in-store pickup this year and is "actively seeking" ways to expand in the U.S., despite a sales boom that has yet to translate to profits, according to recent regulatory filings.
X
Elsewhere in marijuana stocks news, Canadian Canopy Growth Corp. ( CGC ) on Wednesday announced plans to enter the marijuana market in Africa.
Canopy, which already trades in Canada, debuted on the New York Stock Exchange last week. MedMen went public in Canada on Tuesday.
MedMen, in a regulatory filing in Canada dated May 28, said it "plans to engage in delivery operations either through the development of its own delivery infrastructure and network or through the use of third-party services focused on the delivery and e-commerce market."
The company added: "An in-store pickup option is currently being developed in-house and will be accessible from MedMen's website."
The company has stated its plans to offer delivery in other recent filings as well. Daniel Yi, a spokesman for the company, said MedMen has applied for delivery and other new licenses in areas across California. Other details, like where a delivery operation might debut or how it would work, were not available.
The company's regulatory disclosures in Canada offer a deeper look into its strategy and finances. Medical marijuana is legal in Canada, and recreational legalization is set to take hold this year. The U.S. federal government still prohibits marijuana, even as more states vote to make it legal.
The plans come as MedMen rolls out dispensaries in California, Nevada and New York that resemble Apple ( AAPL ) stores and wellness retail locations. A delivery option would mirror those of other retailers, in the fully legal world of retail, banking on delivery and online ordering.
MedMen, in the filing, also said it is "actively seeking additional acquisition opportunities in its existing markets and additional key markets such as Illinois, Florida, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Ohio."

Please contact customer service CLOSE MedMen: $31 Million Net Loss, 760.4% Sales Gain MedMen reported a combined total of $6 million in sales for all of 2017 and the latter half of 2016, according to regulatory disclosures. But during that time, it racked up a net loss of nearly $31 million.
Still, during the final quarter of last year, sales surged 760.4% from a year earlier to $1.46 million. MedMen attributed the gain to strong retail sales and the acquisition of dispensaries in California and New York last year. But costs also rose, due to the operating expenses for those dispensaries and the addition of new employees.
"Over the past two years, execution on our expansion strategy and driving revenue growth has taken priority over improving our gross margin," MedMen said in the May 28 filing.
It added that "as our retail footprint increases and our cultivation and production facilities become fully productive, we expect our gross margin to improve as we leverage our distribution power."
Yi said the company was "very much on a growth pattern" and that the losses shouldn't be a surprise. He also said the figures don't reflect recreational marijuana sales in California, where recreational legalization began in January.
"None of those numbers capture what happens and what will happen in California," he said.
Canopy Growth Heads To Africa While U.S. marijuana companies look toward new states and toward Canada, Canadian marijuana companies are increasingly looking abroad.
Canopy Growth on Wednesday said it had acquired a company called Highlands, which is based in the Kingdom of Lesotho, a mountainous enclave nation that sits within South Africa. Highlands has a license to cultivate cannabis and its resin.
Lesotho legalized medical marijuana last year, making it the first nation in Africa to do so. Canopy said the nation, with its sunny climate and high-altitude geography, had "ideal humidity and growing conditions for greenhouse cultivation."
"Together with very low operating and resource costs, this places Canopy Growth in a position to produce large quantities of high-quality medical cannabis at a low cost," Canopy said in a statement.
The company added that its goal was "future local production to serve the regional market." Canopy also said the move would help Lesotho's economy, in part by creating jobs.
Canopy rose 2.35% in the stock market today . Cronos Group ( CRON ), which listed on the Nasdaq in February, was up 6%.
